THE FOUR PILLARS
iARM Framework Overview
The iARM framework unifies reliability engineering and financial governance through four interlocking pillars: Quantify, Prioritize, Mitigate, and Communicate — each turning raw operational data into capital decisions.
PILLAR 1 · DATA FOUNDATION
ERP Event Data Input
Historical failure events are ingested directly from the plant ERP system. Each record captures downtime hours, production loss, parts, labor, environmental, regulatory, and safety costs — the raw material for all downstream risk quantification.
PILLAR 1 · QUANTIFICATION
Poisson Frequency Model
Annual event counts are modeled as a Poisson process with rate λ = 50.034, derived from observed failure history. The distribution explicitly captures year-to-year frequency variability rather than suppressing it behind a single average.
PILLAR 1 · QUANTIFICATION
Lognormal Severity Distribution
Per-event cost is modeled as Lognormal(μ = 12.64, σ = 0.4899). The CV is calculated from ERP cost records — not assumed. The right-skewed tail represents rare, high-consequence events that drive disproportionate financial exposure.
PILLAR 1 · QUANTIFICATION
Annual Loss Distribution
10,000 Monte Carlo simulations produce the compound annual loss distribution. EAL, VaR, and TVaR thresholds at P80 and P95 are annotated directly — exposing the gap between average budgeting targets and true tail risk.
PILLAR 2 · PRIORITIZATION
Asset Tail Driver Analysis
Assets are ranked by their contribution to worst-case annual loss years, not average spend. CDU pump assets with 100% tail hit rates dominate portfolio risk — a concentration invisible to MTBF-based maintenance prioritization.
PILLARS 3 & 4 · MITIGATE · COMMUNICATE
Mitigation ROI & OpEx Reserve
$700K in targeted mitigations reduces mean annual cost by $6.9M, VaR(P80) by $7.6M, and delivers a Tail ROI of 11.67x with a 5-year NPV of $26.9M — expressed in the financial vocabulary capital committees require.
